lastSweep.newSearchOutcome: Reviewed Massive.com official Python client (formerly Polygon.io). No production dependency promoted. Added as BUILD_SANDBOX candidate for tape/streaming and filing-disclosure benchmark; current production lane starvation was addressed independently with reserved multi-lane quote capacity.

candidates.purpose: Official US market REST/WebSocket client with stock trades/quotes plus newer SEC 8-K disclosure endpoints
candidates.latencySuitability: HIGH with paid real-time entitlement; benchmark required against current Yahoo/Finviz cadence
candidates.maintenance: Official SDK; latest visible commit 2026-07-09 added 8-K disclosure/taxonomy endpoints. README documents REST and WebSocket stock feeds and explicit development test/lint commands.
candidates.securityNotes: Requires vendor API key. Keep credentials server-side only. WebSocket client authenticates after TLS connection and has bounded reconnect/resubscribe logic; still require secret rotation, connection metrics and vendor outage fallback.
candidates.lookAheadRisk: LOW for live trade/quote messages when vendor event timestamps are persisted; historical/replay use must preserve source event time and must not backfill later disclosures into earlier snapshots.
candidates.reason: Strong official WebSocket implementation includes reconnect count, resubscription reconciliation and wildcard tape subscriptions; also exposes last/list trades and quotes and recently added 8-K disclosures. Direct production integration depends on paid real-time entitlement, latency/coverage benchmark, reconnect behavior under load, and reconciliation against an independent source.

candidates.purpose: Real-time US equities WebSocket market data and paper/broker adapter
candidates.latencySuitability: HIGH if entitled feed is available
candidates.securityNotes: Requires API credentials and strict secret handling; sandbox/paper keys available. Do not expose keys to browser.
candidates.lookAheadRisk: LOW for live streaming; historical benchmarking must pin event timestamps and feed entitlement.
candidates.reason: Strong official StockDataStream pattern, typed validation, documented streaming clients. Production integration depends on data entitlement and benchmark against current cadence.

candidates.purpose: SEC/EDGAR parsing, filings, financials and catalyst extraction
candidates.securityNotes: Must identify SEC requests correctly and rate-limit; parse untrusted filing HTML in isolated process if expanded to rendering.
candidates.lookAheadRisk: LOW if filing acceptance/filed timestamps are preserved; HIGH if later facts are backfilled into earlier snapshots.
candidates.reason: Strong candidate for Catalyst Clock and dilution/financing challenger, but must benchmark parsing latency and timestamp fidelity before production.

candidates.purpose: Semantic SEC HTML parsing into element trees with explicit parser/test tooling
candidates.latencySuitability: MEDIUM; parser layer rather than filing-discovery transport
candidates.maintenance: Repository remains maintained but commit cadence is moderate; latest visible commit 2026-06-25, prior functional merge 2025-03-25.
candidates.securityNotes: Treat filing HTML as untrusted input; run parser in bounded process and retain accession/source URL plus parser warnings. Repository includes code coverage, pre-commit, typing and contribution tooling.
candidates.lookAheadRisk: LOW if original filing acceptance timestamp and accession are retained; semantic parsing must never use amended/later filing text for an earlier event snapshot.
candidates.reason: Useful semantic-tree and parser-failure-isolation patterns, MIT license and visible test/quality tooling. Less attractive than EdgarTools as a direct dependency because maintenance cadence is slower and it does not solve low-latency filing discovery itself.

candidates.purpose: Multi-provider financial-data normalization and provider abstraction patterns
candidates.latencySuitability: MEDIUM; useful abstraction layer, not preferred as the lowest-latency scanner core
candidates.maintenance: Active; current develop branch and broad provider ecosystem
candidates.securityNotes: Large dependency/provider surface; credentials may span multiple vendors. Keep provider secrets server-side and sandbox each connector.
candidates.lookAheadRisk: MEDIUM because normalized downstream datasets may combine providers with different timestamps; event-time provenance must be preserved explicitly.
candidates.reason: README documents a connect-once/consume-everywhere provider abstraction, but AGPLv3, large dependency surface and the project's own data-accuracy disclaimer make direct TAGX production integration unattractive. Borrow provider-interface and provenance patterns only.

candidates.latencySuitability: Pattern suitable; current implementation is Binance-specific
candidates.securityNotes: No production dependency recommended until license/tests are verified.
candidates.lookAheadRisk: LOW if receive timestamps and sequence order are retained
candidates.reason: Useful event-log and monotonic replay architecture for T-5/T-15/T-30/T-60 reconstruction, not directly suitable for US equities ingestion.

candidates.purpose: Event-driven backtesting and explicit look-ahead-bias controls
candidates.latencySuitability: LOW for live scanner; useful research pattern
candidates.securityNotes: Large framework dependency surface; avoid direct production coupling.
candidates.reason: Adopt event-time and anti-look-ahead design concepts rather than integrate the full framework.

candidates.purpose: Recent official market-data SDK used to inspect WebSocket subscription, retry and reconnect test patterns
candidates.latencySuitability: NOT APPLICABLE to TAGX US equities; useful implementation pattern only
candidates.maintenance: Active; release 0.16.0 prepared 2026-08-25 and live-trades WebSocket support added 2026-07-29
candidates.securityNotes: API key is placed in the WebSocket URL in current tests; TAGX must not copy that credential transport pattern. Reusable parts are batching, disconnect simulation and retry/backoff testing only.
candidates.lookAheadRisk: LOW for live tape patterns if event timestamps are preserved
candidates.reason: Official SDK has explicit WebSocket tests for batching, disconnects, auth errors and retries, but it serves Tadawul rather than US equities. Borrow resilience-test patterns only; do not integrate as a TAGX data source.
